newsitem.title: USA: Premier, Baxter Allegiance ink supply pact.
newsitem.headline: Premier, Baxter Allegiance ink supply pact.

text.p: A corporate partnership between Premier, Baxter Healthcare Corp and Allegiance Corp should solidify Allegiance's independence in the wake of its spin-off from Baxter International Inc last month, health care industry analysts said.

Premier, the nation's largest alliance of hospitals and healthcare systems, said on Monday that it will buy medical and surgical supplies from Baxter and Allegiance as part of a seven-year supply pact. Premier said the deal, which analysts said had been in the works for months, could generate sales of as much as $1 billion annually.
Eli Kammerman, an analyst at Salomon Brothers, said the supply agreement helps cement Baxter's recent corporate shift that included the Allegiance spin-off.
"The deal positions Allegiance as a premier hospital supply provider," Kammerman explained, "and allows Baxter to reposition itself to become a high-tech focus company."
The spin-off left Baxter as a market leader in technologies related to blood and circulatory systems, including intravenous systems and renal products.
The Premier agreement is one of the first for Allegiance since the spin-off. Allegiance, based in Evanston, Ill., will serve as Deerfield-based Baxter's primary distributor.

The corporate partnership covers group purchasing agreements for a variety of products, including intravenous solutions, drug delivery systems, and surgical and respiratory therapy products. It will go into effect February 1, 1997.

Charlotte, N.C.-based Premier was created from a merger of American Health Systems Inc, SunHealth Alliance and Premier Health Alliance Inc. The company serves the 250 owners of 700 hospitals and health care facilities and more than 1,100 affiliated hospitals and health care organizations nationwide.
